text: By 2030, many experts believe that artificial intelligence will become far more integrated into our daily lives. While we already have narrow AI that excels at specific tasks, the true goal is Artificial General Intelligence, or AGI. AGI would match human cognitive abilities across any domain, from writing poetry to conducting scientific research. The potential benefits are enormous: AGI could solve climate change, cure diseases, and revolutionize education. However, risks exist, including job displacement, ethical misuse, and even loss of human control. Predictions vary wildly—some say AGI arrives by 2045, others believe it may take a century or never happen at all. What is certain is that we must develop careful safeguards as we approach this transformative milestone.
